nodes.description: PLCB3 converts phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate into inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate and diacylglycerol, the two second messengers of the phosphoinositide pathway. Reduced hydrolysis leaves PIP2 elevated. PIP2 is not only a precursor but a direct regulator of actin-binding proteins at the plasma membrane, which is how a signalling-enzyme defect becomes a cytoskeletal one.

nodes.description: The c.2632G>T variant substitutes a serine for a highly conserved alanine in the Ha2' element of the proximal C-terminal domain. That element normally docks against the catalytic core; disrupting the contact destabilises the whole protein. The lesion is therefore not in the active site but in an intramolecular interface that the active site depends on.

evidence.snippet: The identified variant (c.2632G>T) substitutes a serine for a highly conserved alanine within the Ha2' element of the proximal C-terminal domain. This disrupts binding of the Ha2' element to the catalytic core and destabilises PLCB3.

nodes.description: The demonstrated cellular endpoint. Chondrocytes depend on actin organisation for their shape, their columnar arrangement in the growth plate and their mechanotransduction, and corneal stromal keratocytes depend on it for the lamellar collagen order that keeps the cornea clear - which makes this a plausible common route to the skeletal and corneal phenotypes, although the connection has not been shown in either tissue.
